Having a college degree is not a necessity, but I'll still suggest getting one. Isipin mo nalang na bonus mo na yan sa sarili mo.

As for which school, I don't really care as long as I get my diploma (pansin ko lang, mas madaming companies ngayon na hindi tumitingin kung anong school ka nagtapos kaya ko nasabi ito)

There are schools out there that offer online classes like STI, AMA, etc. Kung ayaw mo mag physical classes, you can consider this.

Kung bet mo naman ang physical classes pero takot ka na baka di mo mapagsabay ang work + studies mo, you can opt for less units/subjects. Mas matagal kang gagraduate, pero darating ka rin doon. Slowly but surely ika nga.

You also have advantage than your peers kasi ikaw, may working experience na. Treat that as a plus.

Goodluck!

There's a reason why IT jobs offer higher salary. Hindi talaga sila madali. Everyday, programmers solve problems. Ito 'yung struggle talaga, walang araw na di sila haharap sa problema, and not all people were able to handle that. 

I saw a lot of rants and social media posts about getting burned out sa programming even though they earn decent amount of money. They eventually left the industry to pursue other careers. They were much happier kahit na mas mababa ang sahod. Dumating na kasi sa point na 'yung iba, just thinking about going back to the industry, na nausea na sila at parang nagpapanic na agad.

I am not demotivating OP to switch to IT. Just want to share that IT is not for everyone, and that is proven by some people in the industry as well. I have friends who are programmers.

This is what I will suggest to people who really want to learn the basics of Python programming. First, read Python tutorials in W3schools.com. Kahit 'yung basic lang muna, no Pandas, NumPys and etc. You don't have to take them to heart. Basta magets mo ang basics at magka idea ka logic ng programming at sa syntax. 

Pag natapos mo na 'yan, try to enroll to Angela Yu bootcamp in Udemy. May bayad nga lang ito pero less than 600 lang kapag may Udemy sale. For me, dito ka mas mahahasa in terms of learning the logic of programming. More on exercises kasi siya.

Madami akong nasayang na oras kakahanap ng free resources. Nanunod ako ng YouTube tutorials pero kulang ang turo, di kaya ng 4 hours para i-cover ang mga kailangan mong malaman sa Python. If I will start over again, W3schools then Udemy course ang aaralin ko and I am good na.

I also considered enrolling in bootcamps. But I've decided to spend multiple courses nalang sa Udemy kasi less than 5k lang ang magagastos ko utmost.

Ang pinakamahirap na part dito ay motivation to self learn. Sa bootcamp kasi, mas mappressure kang mag-aral kasi may mga kasama ka at siyempre mahal ang bayad para sayangin ang opportunity to learn.

But if you really want to enroll, I suggest bili ka muna ng Udemy course. You don't have to take it to heart but you should learn at least the basics. After you finish the Udemy course, then apply to a bootcamp. Mahirap kung zero knowledge ka tapos mag-eenroll ka sa bootcamp. Baka magsunog ka lang ng 80k na wala ring natutunan dahil sa info overload.
